britten.title: The analysis of visual motion: a comparison of neuronal and psychophysical performance
britten.finding: In stochastic-motion discrimination, sensitivity of many individual MT neurons approached behavioral sensitivity when stimuli were tailored to the recorded neuron. The study compared neuronal and behavioral discrimination on the same task.

salzman.title: Cortical microstimulation influences perceptual judgements of motion direction
salzman.finding: Electrical stimulation of direction-selective MT clusters biased reported motion toward the preferred direction of the stimulated population, linking a characterized sensory code to a perceptual decision.

devalois_o.title: The orientation and direction selectivity of cells in macaque visual cortex
devalois_o.finding: Striate neurons exhibited a broad distribution of orientation bandwidths and both direction-selective and direction-insensitive responses. Orientation and motion selectivity were measured as tuning properties of individual cells.

harrison.title: Decoding reveals the contents of visual working memory in early visual areas
harrison.finding: Human fMRI patterns in V1-V4 identified the remembered grating orientation during a blank delay, including cases with little sustained average activation. Information in a population pattern could persist despite low mean activity.

mcadams.title: Effects of attention on orientation-tuning functions of single neurons in macaque cortical area V4
mcadams.finding: During an orientation attention task, V4 responses increased with attention largely through scaling of tuning curves, without a systematic change in tuning width. V1 modulation was smaller.

legge.title: Contrast masking in human vision
legge.finding: Human grating discrimination showed facilitation at weak masking contrasts and increased thresholds at stronger masks. A nonlinear contrast transducer, spatial filtering and pooling explained the dependence on masker strength and frequency.

reynolds00.title: Attention increases sensitivity of V4 neurons
reynolds00.finding: Attention increased V4 responses more strongly at low than high stimulus contrast. The pattern was consistent with an increase in effective contrast, connecting attentional state with sensory sensitivity.

normalization.title: The normalization model of attention
normalization.finding: An attention field modulates stimulus drive before a shared suppressive normalization. Changing stimulus size and attentional spread changes whether predicted responses resemble contrast gain, response gain or other modulation patterns.

campbell.title: Application of Fourier analysis to the visibility of gratings
campbell.finding: Thresholds for several grating waveforms were explained by the visibility of their Fourier components. Higher harmonics became behaviorally useful when they exceeded their own thresholds, supporting frequency-selective visual mechanisms.

devalois_f.title: Spatial frequency selectivity of cells in macaque visual cortex
devalois_f.finding: Measurements of striate neurons revealed many narrow spatial-frequency bandwidths and a wide range of preferred frequencies at a given eccentricity, supporting multiple spatial-frequency channels.

regan.title: Spatial-frequency discrimination and detection: comparison of postadaptation thresholds
regan.finding: Adaptation altered frequency-discrimination and grating-detection thresholds differently. The dissociation supported a distinction between detecting channel activity and comparing relative responses across overlapping channels.

derrington.title: Chromatic mechanisms in lateral geniculate nucleus of macaque
derrington.finding: Color-space null measurements characterized how LGN neurons combine cone signals. The results exposed opponent chromatic mechanisms and separated chromatic from luminance-dependent response directions.

lennie.title: Chromatic mechanisms in striate cortex of macaque
lennie.finding: V1 neurons responded to combinations of chromatic and luminance modulation. Their distribution of preferred color directions differed from the more distinctly grouped LGN mechanisms, showing a cortical transformation of cone-derived signals.

flanagan.title: Independent orientation-selective mechanisms for the cardinal directions of colour space
flanagan.finding: Opposite tilt aftereffects could be induced for chromatic and luminance gratings. The psychophysical dissociation supported orientation-selective mechanisms operating on multiple chromatic and achromatic signals.

field.title: Contour integration by the human visual system: evidence for a local association field
field.finding: People detected paths made of aligned Gabor elements within randomly oriented backgrounds. Detection depended strongly on the alignment and continuation of neighboring elements, motivating an association field linking compatible local orientations.

kapadia.title: Improvement in visual sensitivity by changes in local context: parallel studies in human observers and in V1 of alert monkeys
kapadia.finding: Collinear context improved human bar detection and facilitated responses in a subset of monkey V1 neurons. Relative position, orientation and intervening elements controlled the contextual effect.

li.title: Contour saliency in primary visual cortex
li.finding: During contour detection, V1 responses tracked contour salience and were weaker when contours were missed or unattended. Neural discrimination connected contextual responses with perceptual performance.

tolhurst97.title: Discrimination of changes in the slopes of the amplitude spectra of natural images: band-limited contrast and psychometric functions
tolhurst97.finding: Sensitivity to spectral-slope changes could be explained by contrast changes within limited frequency bands. Which band was informative depended on the reference spectrum, linking global-looking judgments to selective spatial filtering.

tolhurst00.title: Discrimination of spectrally blended natural images: optimisation of the human visual system for encoding natural images
tolhurst00.finding: Experiments blending photograph spectra found enhanced sensitivity around natural spectral statistics after controlling image properties. The manipulation tested natural-image specialization more directly than successful discrimination of arbitrary slopes alone.

olshausen.title: Emergence of simple-cell receptive field properties by learning a sparse code for natural images
olshausen.finding: Learning a sparse representation of natural image patches produced localized, oriented, bandpass basis functions. The theory connects environmental statistics to an efficient sensory representation.

griffin.title: Orienting attention to locations in internal representations
griffin.finding: Cues presented before or after a visual array improved recognition of relevant locations. Behavioral and electrophysiological results linked orienting in perception and memory while revealing differences between precue and retrocue processing.

kiani.title: Bounded integration in parietal cortex underlies decisions even when viewing duration is dictated by the environment
kiani.finding: Monkeys could commit to a motion choice before externally controlled viewing ended. LIP activity supported accumulation to a bound, demonstrating that late available evidence need not influence the decision.

stine.title: Differentiating between integration and non-integration strategies in perceptual decision making
stine.finding: Task manipulations distinguished prolonged evidence integration from nonintegration strategies that can reproduce common behavioral signatures. Most tested observers showed evidence for prolonged integration under the diagnostic design.

mante.title: Context-dependent computation by recurrent dynamics in prefrontal cortex
mante.finding: Monkeys selected motion or color evidence according to context. Prefrontal population activity and trained recurrent-network dynamics linked context-dependent selection with evidence integration.

lovejoy.title: Inactivation of primate superior colliculus impairs covert selection of signals for perceptual judgments
lovejoy.finding: SC inactivation shifted motion judgments away from signals in the affected field toward competing information elsewhere. Deficits depended strongly on informative distractors; affecting the foil location favored judgments based on the cued signal.

bollimunta.title: Comparing frontal eye field and superior colliculus contributions to covert spatial attention
bollimunta.finding: Reversible FEF and SC inactivation impaired covert motion-change detection. Comparing the two interventions in a shared behavioral framework tested their contributions to selection during maintained fixation.

arcizet.title: Covert spatial selection in primate basal ganglia
arcizet.finding: Monkeys detected cued motion changes with a joystick while maintaining fixation. Caudate neurons encoded relevant location and task epoch, extending spatial-selection signals beyond overt orienting movements.

zenon.title: Attention deficits without cortical neuronal deficits
zenon.finding: SC inactivation impaired attentive behavior while established attentional modulation in visual cortex persisted. Behavioral selection and cortical response enhancement could therefore dissociate.

wheeler.title: Binding in short-term visual memory
wheeler.finding: Change-detection experiments separated memory for features from memory for their combinations. Binding was vulnerable to interference, motivating a distinction between retained feature information and attention-dependent integration.

bays.title: The precision of visual working memory is set by allocation of a shared resource
bays.finding: Continuous-report errors reflected both feature and location memory. Accounting for their joint uncertainty supported a shared-resource description in which precision changes with the number of remembered objects.

miller93.title: Activity of neurons in anterior inferior temporal cortex during a short-term memory task
miller93.finding: IT responses carried match-related information during delayed matching. Stimulus-selective delay activity could be disrupted by intervening stimuli, separating visible delay activity from successful later recognition.

miller96.title: Neural mechanisms of visual working memory in prefrontal cortex of the macaque
miller96.finding: A delayed matching task with intervening test objects examined prefrontal signals for remembered samples and matching decisions. It provided a comparison with temporal-cortex mechanisms under interference.

basso.title: Modulation of neuronal activity in superior colliculus by changes in target probability
basso.finding: SC buildup activity varied with target probability, including when probability changed while the display remained fixed. More possible targets reduced preparatory activity, linking selection state with uncertainty and saccade latency.

competition.title: Competitive mechanisms subserve attention in macaque areas V2 and V4
competition.finding: For two stimuli within a receptive field, attention shifted the response toward that evoked by the attended item alone. The findings supported biased competition between simultaneously represented stimuli.

cohen.title: Attention improves performance primarily by reducing interneuronal correlations
cohen.finding: Population recordings in V4 during an orientation-change task linked much of the attentional improvement in population sensitivity to reduced shared variability, beyond changes in average firing rates.

chelazzi.title: A neural basis for visual search in inferior temporal cortex
chelazzi.finding: Monkeys remembered a picture and selected its match from a small array. IT showed sample-related delay activity, followed during search by suppression of nontarget responses and dominance of the target representation.

soto.title: Early, involuntary top-down guidance of attention from working memory
soto.finding: A remembered colored shape facilitated line search when it surrounded the target and impaired search when it surrounded a distractor. Effects extended to early responses and the first saccade.

bichot.title: Parallel and serial neural mechanisms for visual search in macaque area V4
bichot.finding: During free visual search, V4 responses favored objects sharing target features across the display. The experiment related feature-based parallel bias to selection during search among complex items.

wolfe.title: Guided Search 6.0: An updated model of visual search
wolfe.finding: Guidance combines stimulus features, target goals, history, reward and scene information into a changing priority map. Selection guides the order in which objects receive further processing and recognition.

schall.title: Neural basis of saccade target selection in frontal eye field during visual search
schall.finding: Initial FEF visual responses did not distinguish target from distractor. Activity subsequently evolved to identify the target before the eye movement, separating stimulus onset responses from selection.

zaksas.title: Directional signals in the prefrontal cortex and in area MT during a working memory for visual motion task
zaksas.finding: Monkeys compared two motion directions across a delay. MT and PFC carried direction information with transient delay signals; test responses depended on the remembered sample and related to the eventual decision.

ling.title: How spatial and feature-based attention affect the gain and tuning of population responses
ling.finding: External-noise motion experiments separated spatial from feature-based attention. Threshold-versus-noise functions supported different combinations of population gain and tuning, giving behavioral tests of attentional mechanisms.

stokes.title: Dynamic coding for cognitive control in prefrontal cortex
stokes.finding: Population analyses examined how prefrontal coding changed while establishing, maintaining and using task context. The study motivates measuring representational transformations through time rather than only mean persistent activation.
